title: Hard cutover: remove legacy backend manifest kind ocaml-cmxs
description:
Enforce hard-cutover compatibility policy by removing deprecated backend manifest kind alias `ocaml-cmxs`. Only `haxe-provider` and `ocaml-dynlink` remain valid kinds.

Scope:
- remove parser fallback/normalization from ocaml-cmxs -> ocaml-dynlink
- remove deprecated warning path and references
- update manifest schema enum to drop ocaml-cmxs
- update docs and tests to reflect strict behavior

Acceptance:
- test:m14:backend-plugin-manifest passes with ocaml-cmxs rejected
- docs mention only ocaml-dynlink
- ci:guards passes

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Implemented hard cutover for backend manifest kind alias removal. Changes: parser now accepts only haxe-provider + ocaml-dynlink (no ocaml-cmxs normalization/warning path), build-backend-plugin CLI no longer accepts ocaml-cmxs, schema enum removed ocaml-cmxs, promotion host adapter docs now list ocaml-dynlink-only policy, and manifest integration test now asserts ocaml-cmxs is rejected. TDD: updated test first and confirmed fail, then implemented change. Validation: npm run -s test:m14:backend-plugin-manifest, npm run -s test:hxhx:promotion-backend-smoke, npm run ci:guards all pass. Follow-up created for bootstrap snapshot parity refresh: haxe.ocaml-i9m6.

title: hxhx native frontend: surface header-only fallback as protocol flag
description: When HXHX_NATIVE_FRONTEND_HEADER_ONLY triggers, the native parser currently returns ok + header AST but there is no explicit signal that a fallback occurred. Add an optional v=1 record like: ast header_only <len>:<payload> (payload is 0 or 1) and propagate it into the Haxe-side HxModuleDecl so Stage3 can count/report how many modules were header-only. Update docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_NATIVE_FRONTEND_PROTOCOL.md accordingly.

title: Run mainstream Haxe compatibility gates after source-lane fixes

- Documented gate command set for local/CI: npm run test:upstream:unit-macro-stage3-no-emit, npm run test:upstream:runci-macro-stage3-direct, npm run test:upstream:display-stage3-no-emit, and npm run test:upstream:replacement-ready:strict

title: Stage3 resolver: infer std classpath from .haxerc/Lix when env unset
description:
Problem
- Stage3 compiler invocation from a stage0-free hxhx binary fails to resolve std modules when HAXE_STD_PATH/HAXEPATH are unset.
- Repro: hxhx --target ocaml-stage3 ... -main hxhx.Main currently fails with import_missing haxe.io.Path.

Goal
- Make Stage1Args/Stage3 classpath bootstrap infer std root from repo/workspace .haxerc + default Lix install layout, without requiring HAXE_STD_PATH to be exported manually.

Acceptance
- New integration test proves Stage1Args.parse appends inferred std root when env vars are unset and .haxerc points to an installed Lix version.
- Stage3 invocation no longer immediately fails with import_missing haxe.io.Path in this environment classpath bootstrap path.
- No Any/Dynamic usage added.
close_reason: Implemented Stage1 std-root inference from .haxerc + Lix HOME layouts and added regression coverage (test:m14:stage1-std-root-inference). Follow-up haxe.ocaml-chqs tracks end-to-end binary validation after source-lane rebuild.

title: Harden Gate1 unit typeonly/emit haxelib resolution
description: Apply the same deterministic haxelib precompute used by Gate1 no-emit to the Stage3 type-only and emit runners for compile-macro.hxml. Generate tests/unit/haxe_libraries/utest.hxml from haxelib path output with retries on transient exit 244 so Stage3 lib resolution is robust in CI.
notes: Implemented in scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-stage3-typeonly.sh and scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-unit-macro-stage3-emit.sh. Added prepare_haxelib_hxml helper that runs haxelib --always path utest, retries transient exit 244 up to 3 attempts, and writes tests/unit/haxe_libraries/utest.hxml with normalized -cp/-D/--macro lines before invoking Stage3. Validation: type-only runner passes with a flaky HAXELIB_BIN wrapper that forces first path call to exit 244. Emit runner progresses through macro/lib resolution with same wrapper; current local failure is later in emit build (String.make unbound in generated OCaml), unrelated to haxelib resolution path.

title: Stage3: parse try/catch expression blocks
description: Stage3 no-emit diagnostics still report one unsupported expr in upstream tests/sourcemaps/Test.hx due to the expression form: var x = try { ... } catch(...) { ... }. Add minimal expression parsing/lowering so this shape is represented in the HxExpr tree without EUnsupported (even if semantics are placeholder initially).
acceptance_criteria: - HXHX_TRACE_UNSUPPORTED=1 npm run test:upstream:runci-macro-stage3-driver reports unsupported_exprs_total=0\n- Add repo-local fixture covering try/catch expression parsing (no upstream code copied)\n- Document any semantic limitations of the placeholder lowering

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-02-07: Implemented Stage3 parsing support for try/catch in expression position by introducing HxExpr.ETryCatchRaw (token-rendered placeholder) and teaching HxParser to consume try { ... } catch(...) { ... } without producing EUnsupported('try'). This avoids an OCaml bootstrap dependency cycle (HxExpr <-> HxStmt) while eliminating the last Gate2 stage3_no_emit unsupported expr in upstream sourcemaps. Added a repo-local Stage3 no-emit regression in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.

title: Fix OCaml dispatch wrapper typing for Iterator-return methods
description:
Portable fixture work for haxe.ds-01 exposed a stage0 OCaml emission mismatch on dispatch-record method fields.

Observed failure:
- In generated `haxe_ds_BalancedTree.ml`, field `keys` is typed to return `Obj.t` but wrapper body returns `Haxe_iterators_ArrayIterator.t`.
- dune fails in strict portable lane with type mismatch.

Reproducer:
- Compile a fixture that references `haxe.ds.BalancedTree` with:
  - `-D ocaml_build=native`
  - `-D ocaml_portable_native_surface=error`
acceptance_criteria: - Reproducer fixture using haxe.ds.BalancedTree compiles in strict portable lane\n- Generated dispatch field wrappers are type-consistent with record field signatures\n- No new warning-as-error regressions in existing m6/m14 suites
notes: Added M6 regression coverage via test/BalancedTreeDispatchMain.hx and test/M6BalancedTreeDispatchIntegrationTest.hx; fixed dispatch wrapper bridging in packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/reflaxe/ocaml/OcamlCompiler.hx so strict dune builds no longer fail on BalancedTree iterator-return wrappers.
close_reason: Added M6 regression ( + ) and fixed dispatch wrapper bridging in  so strict dune build no longer fails on  iterator-return wrappers.

title: Narrow Dynamic usage in Stage3 backend dispatch
description:
Problem
- `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend` still uses `backendDyn:Dynamic` for bridge dispatch, which broadens an internal compiler API path.
- Repo policy forbids broad `Dynamic`/`Any` unless tightly justified at unavoidable runtime boundaries.

Goal
- Reduce `Dynamic` spread in Stage3 backend dispatch while preserving current behavior (including reflaxe bridge compatibility).

Scope
1) Refactor `emitWithBackend` to avoid broad `Dynamic` storage where possible.
2) Keep any unavoidable runtime-boundary cast isolated and documented.
3) Ensure existing backend dispatch behavior remains unchanged.
4) Keep docs updated if boundary policy wording changes.

Acceptance criteria
- `emitWithBackend` no longer stores `backend` as `Dynamic` for general dispatch.
- Bridge dispatch still works for current wrapper-backed backends.
- `test:m14:target-core-wiring`, `test:m14:backend-registry`, and `ci:guards` pass.
close_reason: Stage3 backend dispatch Dynamic scope narrowed; bridge behavior preserved.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented
- Narrowed Stage3 backend dispatch typing in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend`:
  - removed broad `backendDyn:Dynamic` general dispatch variable
  - switched typed bridge checks to `Std.isOfType(backend, ...)` with typed casts per bridge
  - kept `Dynamic` only at the final reflection fallback seam (`backendReflect`) where unavoidable
  - reflection fallback now passes `expandedProgram` (typed) instead of raw `expanded`

Validation
- `npm run -s test:m14:target-core-wiring`
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-registry`
- `npm run ci:guards`

title: Stage3 parity: modulo/static-field and comprehension arithmetic mismatches
description:
While upgrading `hxhx-native-reflaxe-bench` (x02), richer variants exposed Stage3-only mismatches:
- `% modulus` where modulus came from a static field produced OCaml emission equivalent to `Obj.magic 0` in one lane.
- An array/comprehension-heavy arithmetic variant produced `bench_result=0` in stage3 while delegated/interp produced non-zero deterministic output.

Follow-up work:
1) Reduce to minimal repro fixtures (snapshot + portable where possible).
2) Isolate typing/emitter stage where `%`/comprehension path diverges.
3) Fix emission/parity and restore richer bench constructs if stable.
4) Ensure native bench lanes stay output-identical.
notes: Prioritized to P1 as immediate stabilization gate before Phase C execution.
close_reason: Implemented Stage3 arithmetic parity fixes for modulo/comprehension and added regression coverage in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh; source-level Stage3 harness now reproduces expected outputs (sum=15, value=815).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-02-23 reprioritized to P1 as immediate stabilization gate before Phase C execution. Phase C root epic haxe.ocaml-8nv explicitly depends on this bug closure.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented Stage3 emitter parity fixes for modulo/comprehension arithmetic and added a regression case in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh (static-field modulo + comprehension arithmetic).

acceptance_criteria: Stage0 haxe builds stage1 via reflaxe.ocaml; stage1 runs a subset compilation end-to-end.

title: M0 — Project skeleton + Reflaxe wiring
description: Bootstrap + init macros, target registration, and minimal file emission (.ml).
acceptance_criteria: Trivial Haxe program emits at least one compilable .ml file into ocaml_output.

title: Scaffold repo layout + haxelib metadata
description: Create directory/layout per PRD (src/, std/, runtimegen/, test/, haxe_libraries/, haxelib.json).
acceptance_criteria: Project installs via haxelib/dev and compiles macros without missing paths.

title: Implement CompilerBootstrap macro (classpath injection)
description: Early bootstrap macro to inject classpaths safely (pattern from Elixir target).
acceptance_criteria: -lib reflaxe.ocaml reliably finds compiler + std override paths in all invocation modes.

title: Implement CompilerInit macro (ReflectCompiler.AddCompiler)
description: Register OcamlCompiler with Reflaxe/ReflectCompiler.
acceptance_criteria: Target selected when -lib reflaxe.ocaml present; emits output via output iterator.

title: Define target knobs + minimal output iterator
description: Set .ml extension, ocaml_output define, file-per-module, reserved keywords, __ocaml__ injection, minimal OutputIterator.
acceptance_criteria: Main module is written to disk with stable filename + directory.

title: Doc: portable vs ocaml-native surfaces + defines
description: Document the two surfaces (portable stdlib-first vs ocaml-native ocaml.*) and how to mix them.
acceptance_criteria: Docs explain std/_std vs ocaml.* and which defines control behavior.

title: M9 — Haxe-in-Haxe prototype path (stage1)

acceptance_criteria: Stage0 builds stage1 OCaml binary; stage1 runs subset compilation; clear ML2HX integration contract.

title: Create haxe_in_haxe_proto harness

title: Define ML2HX subset contract (lists/options/maps/modules)

acceptance_criteria: Contract doc exists and is referenced by prototype + future translation tooling.

title: Define OcamlAST core nodes

description: Add fixture Haxe inputs and assert emitted .ml compiles.
acceptance_criteria: Test harness can compile output and run basic behavior checks.

title: backend boundary: eliminate GenIrProgram cast leakage
description:
Context
- During `hxhx` Stage3/backend integration, `ITargetCore.emit(program, context)` is typed in Haxe as `program:GenIrProgram`.
- In generated OCaml for dynamic backend dispatch, `program` can degrade to `Obj.t` at the call boundary.
- We observed concrete failures in generated files (`backend_js_JsTargetCore.ml`, `backend_ocaml_OcamlTargetCore.ml`) when typed operations expected `MacroExpandedProgram.t`.
- Current fixes use local `cast` to recover type where needed. This is acceptable short-term but not ideal architecture.

Problem Statement
- The current boundary leaks dynamic typing into target-core implementation code.
- Casts can spread and become fragile, reducing readability and confidence in correctness.
- Generated OCaml type-checking errors can surface late (during bootstrap/build), not at earlier Haxe-check points.

Goal
- Define and implement a robust, explicit boundary strategy for `GenIrProgram` that:
  1) keeps current behavior working,
  2) centralizes dynamic->typed conversion,
  3) prevents cast proliferation,
  4) improves generated OCaml type stability,
  5) remains aligned with MIT clean-room goals (no upstream code copying).

Scope (this task)
1. Design review of 3 candidate approaches:
   - A) Single boundary adapter (`requireProgram(v:Dynamic):GenIrProgram`) used only at wrapper seams.
   - B) API refactor of backend dispatch to preserve static types (avoid reflective/dynamic return path where possible).
   - C) Replace `typedef GenIrProgram = MacroExpandedProgram` with a concrete wrapper type to enforce explicit conversion semantics.
2. Choose a preferred near-term implementation path and a medium-term roadmap.
3. Produce implementation checklist + risk analysis + migration order.
4. Identify required regression tests (Haxe-level and generated OCaml/build-level).
5. Document decision in repo docs (where architecture decisions for backend layering live).

Out of Scope
- Full backend architecture rewrite in one PR.
- Large unrelated refactors across parser/typer/runtime.

Deliverables
- Decision note with chosen approach and rationale.
- Concrete task breakdown for incremental rollout (small, reviewable PRs).
- Tests/gates mapping showing how we validate the boundary.
- Update docs to record the boundary contract and “where casts are allowed” policy.

Suggested Validation Matrix
- `npm run test:m14:target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:m14:js-target-core-wiring`
- `npm run test:hxhx-targets` (or at minimum `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` + js-native smoke lane)
- Any added focused regression test proving generated OCaml no longer fails due `Obj.t`/`MacroExpandedProgram.t` mismatches.

Risk Notes
- Overly aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bring-up.
- Leaving design unresolved will continue causing late bootstrap failures and repeated tactical casts.
acceptance_criteria: A documented boundary decision exists with chosen approach and migration plan; casts are centralized to an explicit boundary helper/pattern (not spread through target cores); targeted wiring tests and at least one end-to-end build/smoke pass validate no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regressions; docs updated to define allowed cast boundary policy.
notes: Implemented near-term boundary decision (Approach B): keep backend and target-core emit APIs statically typed on GenIrProgram, remove local target-core program-cast helpers, and keep casts constrained to narrow Stage3 reflection/bridge seams. Updated docs with explicit policy and roadmap in docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md and docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md; README now references typed provider contract and cast policy. Validation passed: haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser; npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke.

title: Provider boundary cast removal + typed provider registry hardening
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` still uses a scoped boundary cast (`ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch`) because OCaml bootstrap currently mis-lowers direct interface dispatch (`Unbound record field registrations`).
- We removed reflective static registration calls from the hot path, but dynamic provider loading still has one boundary conversion and should be revisited when interface-method OCaml emission is fixed.

Goal
- Remove or further constrain the remaining provider-boundary cast while preserving stage0/stage3 stability and deterministic provider precedence.
- Evaluate whether provider discovery can become fully compile-time typed for builtin providers without losing plugin flexibility.

Scope
1) Re-check interface-method dispatch codegen for `ITargetBackendProvider.registrations()` and attempt a no-cast path.
2) If no-cast is still impossible, keep cast in exactly one helper and add explicit CI guards preventing cast spread.
3) Evaluate provider registration strategies:
   - Option A: static provider table (`providerRegistrations` functions referenced directly at compile time).
   - Option B: macro-generated provider registry (compile-time discovery of known providers).
   - Option C: keep current mixed model (typed known-provider table + dynamic provider loading by type path).
4) Document recommendation with tradeoffs and chosen path.

Pros/Cons to assess
- Static provider table
  Pros: strongest compile-time typing, no reflection for known providers, simple runtime behavior.
  Cons: manual maintenance overhead when new builtin providers are added.
- Macro-generated registry
  Pros: compile-time typing with less manual table upkeep, central source of truth.
  Cons: added macro/build complexity, harder debugging when discovery fails, potential bootstrap coupling risk.
- Mixed model (current)
  Pros: pragmatic, supports plugins today, minimal churn.
  Cons: still has one boundary cast and dynamic edge cases.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision recorded in docs/bead comments with rationale and chosen strategy.
- If cast removed: stage0 build + provider integration tests pass.
- If cast retained: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper, CI guard enforces containment, and tests cover failure diagnostics.
- No broad `Dynamic`/`Any` regressions introduced in resolver/provider path.
close_reason: Cast retained as scoped boundary workaround; CI guardrail + docs + provider tests landed for mixed-model strategy.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Decision summary
- Kept the provider-boundary cast in `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` as a scoped workaround.
- Chosen strategy remains mixed-model provider loading:
  1) compile-time known-provider table for bundled builtin providers,
  2) typed dynamic provider loading (`Type.resolveClass` + `Type.createInstance` + `Std.downcast(..., ITargetBackendProvider)`) for plugin/bundled providers.

Why this decision
- The OCaml bootstrap lane still needs one boundary cast for structural dispatch; removing it now regresses provider loading.
- Mixed model keeps deterministic fast-path behavior for builtins while preserving plugin flexibility without introducing macro-registry complexity.

Changes landed
- Added CI guardrail `scripts/ci/provider-boundary-check.js` and wired it into `npm run ci:guards`.
  - Enforces that provider-boundary cast usage stays isolated to `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/BackendProviderResolver.hx`.
  - Enforces exactly one scoped `return cast providerContract;` occurrence in that file.
  - Blocks reintroduction of `Reflect.callMethod` in the provider-boundary resolver.
- Updated docs:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BUILTIN_BACKENDS.md`
  - `docs/02-user-guide/HXHX_BACKEND_LAYERING.md`
  to reflect typed dynamic providers + mixed-model decision and current cast policy.

Tradeoff evaluation recorded
- Static provider table:
  - Pros: strongest compile-time typing, straightforward runtime path.
  - Cons: manual maintenance cost as provider count grows.
- Macro-generated registry:
  - Pros: auto-discovery of known providers.
  - Cons: added macro/build complexity and bootstrap/debug coupling.
- Mixed model (chosen now):
  - Pros: practical balance for current scope, no additional macro infra needed.
  - Cons: one scoped cast remains until interface-dispatch codegen can be fully represented.

Validation
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-provider-resolver`
- `npm run -s test:m14:backend-registry`
- `npm run ci:guards`

  - packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std/runtime/HxString.ml
    - hardened equals with Obj-level guards:
      - exact hx_null pointer checks first
      - Obj.string_tag verification before String.equal

title: Stage3 backend providers: remove reflective registrations path
description:
Problem
- Stage3 currently loads dynamic backend providers by reflecting a static `providerRegistrations()` method from `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` and casting the returned value.
- This keeps `Reflect.callMethod` + array casts on a critical selection path and weakens type safety (especially with our Any/Dynamic minimization policy).

Goal
- Keep provider loading behavior-compatible while tightening typing and reducing reflection usage.

Scope
1) Add a compile-time known-provider table for builtin provider entrypoints (starting with `backend.js.JsBackend`) so known paths avoid reflection entirely.
2) For non-builtin providers, switch from static reflective method calls to typed instance loading:
   - `Type.resolveClass(typePath)` + `Type.createInstance(cls, [])`
   - require `ITargetBackendProvider` and call `registrations()`
   - fail fast with actionable errors if type missing, ctor invalid, or interface not implemented.
3) Keep deterministic registration order and tracing behavior unchanged.
4) Add regression coverage for:
   - known provider path
   - custom provider implementing `ITargetBackendProvider`
   - negative cases (type missing / wrong interface).

Design notes / alternatives
- Option A (preferred now): static provider table + typed instance providers.
  Pros: simple, no macro complexity, immediate type-safety gain, minimal churn.
  Cons: builtin provider table must be maintained manually.
- Option B: macro-generated provider registry (scan known providers at build time).
  Pros: less manual table upkeep.
  Cons: adds macro/build complexity and can obscure resolution/debuggability; defer until provider surface grows.

Acceptance criteria
- Stage3 provider loading no longer uses `Reflect.callMethod(..., providerRegistrations, ...)` for supported paths.
- Builtin provider loading continues to work in `test:hxhx-targets` dynamic-provider lane.
- New tests cover typed provider instance path and failure diagnostics.
- README/docs updated only if user-facing provider contract changes (likely no doc churn needed).

title: Review provider boundary cast in BackendProviderResolver
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` currently returns `cast providerContract` (ITargetBackendProvider -> ProviderDispatch structural view).
- The cast was introduced to avoid OCaml bootstrap failure (`Unbound record field registrations`) when calling `provider.registrations()` through interface-typed dispatch.

Why this needs follow-up
- We need to verify whether this cast can be removed (or replaced with a compile-time-safe adapter) without regressing stage0 bootstrap compatibility.
- The cast sits on a correctness-critical backend/plugin boundary and should remain tightly scoped/documented if it stays.

Investigation scope
- Reproduce/confirm the OCaml failure mode for direct interface dispatch in this path.
- Evaluate alternatives:
  1) backend/runtime support for interface-method dispatch on this boundary,
  2) typed adapter/helper generated at compile time,
  3) structural-provider view without cast (if possible),
  4) keeping cast with stricter guardrails and tests.
- Ensure no fallback to broad `Dynamic`/reflection dispatch in resolver.

Acceptance criteria
- Decision documented in bead comments (keep vs remove cast) with rationale.
- If removed: stage0 `scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh` succeeds and provider resolver tests stay green.
- If kept: cast remains isolated to one boundary helper with explicit docs + regression coverage proving guard behavior.
close_reason: Decision recorded: keep scoped provider-boundary cast for now; validated stage0 bootstrap + provider resolver + target gates after typed catch/ValueException fixes.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Investigation summary
- Reproduced that direct interface dispatch from `ITargetBackendProvider` to `provider.registrations()` emits OCaml record-field access and fails in stage0 bootstrap (`Unbound record field registrations`).
- Confirmed the boundary cast is currently required to switch to structural dispatch (`ProviderDispatch`) while still validating contract via `Std.downcast(..., ITargetBackendProvider)`.

Additional fixes landed
- Added OCaml-target implementation for `haxe.ValueException` (`packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/haxe/ValueException.cross.hx`).
- Added forced type loading for `haxe.ValueException` in OCaml compiler init so typed catch lowering links reliably (`packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src/reflaxe/ocaml/CompilerInit.hx`).
- Kept cast isolated to `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider`.

Validation

title: Gate1: conditional compilation (#if) filtering for resolver
description: Our Stage3 resolver/parser currently ignores conditional compilation directives, so code inside #if blocks (e.g. java/cs/php targets) can be parsed and treated as active. This blocks any attempt to widen the module graph toward real Gate1, and can cause false import_missing failures (e.g. haxe.test.Base).\n\nImplement a minimal, provenance-safe conditional compilation pass that strips inactive blocks before parsing, using Stage3's define set (from -D plus builtin defines like sys/interp).
design:
Implement from scratch (do not port upstream):
- Support: #if <expr>, #elseif <expr>, #else, #end
- Expr subset: identifiers, !, &&, ||, parentheses, ident == "string", ident != "string"
- Define set: parsed -D name[=value] + implicit defines (sys/interp when --interp is present, etc.)
- For unknown identifiers, treat as false (conservative).
- Preserve line count where practical (optional) to keep errors readable.
acceptance_criteria: - Stage3 resolve/parse does not follow imports or type references in inactive #if branches\n- Gate1 bring-up can safely enable same-package type resolution without pulling java/cs/etc-only tests\n- Keep npm test green

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa

Added an 'opaque' directive heuristic for inline one-line constructs (lines starting with # that contain additional # tokens), blanking them without mutating the stack to avoid runaway blanking (fixes utest/utils/Print.hx). Also made Stage3 typing permissive by default (HXHX_TYPER_STRICT=1 re-enables strict errors) so upstream Gate1 native attempt completes: compile-macro.hxml reaches resolved_modules/typed_modules/hook_onGenerate/stage3=no_emit_ok.

title: js-native: add while-statement support (native parser + Stage3 emit)
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently lowers while (...) ... to SExpr(EUnsupported("while"), ...), which causes js-native emit failures (EUnsupported(while)) on valid Haxe code.
- We temporarily adjusted the inc/dec smoke fixture to avoid while, but this leaves a core language gap for JS parity.

Scope
1) Add structured while statement support in Hx AST (HxStmt) and native parser (HxParser.parseStmt).
2) Ensure Stage3 typer handles the new stmt variant in statement traversal/typing.
3) Add js-native lowering in JsStmtEmitter for while loops.
4) Keep non-js paths compiling; for OCaml emitter either implement lowering or fail with explicit typed unsupported message (no silent fallback).
5) Add/expand smoke coverage so a js-native while-loop program compiles and runs in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.

Constraints
- Maintain MIT clean-room approach; behavior-driven implementation only.
- Avoid introducing Dynamic/Any in core logic.
- Keep parser + emitter changes minimal and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria:
- while no longer parses as EUnsupported(while) in native parser statement bodies.
- js-native target compiles and runs a fixture with while loops and correct output.
- npm run -s test:hxhx-targets remains green.
- Any target-specific limitations are explicit and documented (no silent degradation).
notes: Implemented while-statement support end-to-end for current Stage3/js-native path: (1) added SWhile(cond, body, pos) to HxStmt; (2) native parser now parses while (...) body into SWhile instead of EUnsupported(while); (3) typer + macro stmt rewriter + Stage3 unsupported counters recurse through SWhile; (4) js-native statement emitter lowers SWhile to JS while-loops; (5) OCaml Stage3 emitter recursion/dependency walkers and statement lowering now handle SWhile, preserving buildability. Validation: haxe --no-output native parser compile smoke, HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh, and HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets (green).
close_reason: While statements now parse/type/emit in Stage3 and full target suite is green.

title: Spike: family portable|metal consolidation alignment for hxhx/reflaxe.ocaml
description:
## Why
hxhx/reflaxe.ocaml already has strong profile and runtime-slicing foundations. This spike aligns it to the family contract and identifies where inference/reporting should be hardened.

## Inputs
- Existing OCaml profile/runtime references:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/OCAML_PROFILE_CONTRACT.md`
  - `packages/hxhx-core/src/backend/OcamlProfile.hx`

  - `../haxe.go/docs/phase2-roadmap.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/hxrt-selective-runtime.md`

## Spike Scope
1. Compare current OCaml profile/runtime model against family portable|metal contract.
2. Evaluate replacing brittle runtime inference paths with compiler-tracked feature usage where feasible.
3. Define required contract/report artifacts:
   - profile contract report
   - runtime plan report
4. Define migration-safe metal fallback diagnostics policy (where appropriate).

## Deliverables
- Spike doc with:
  - gap analysis
  - hardening plan
  - phased implementation checklist
- Follow-up beads tasks linked to `haxe.ocaml-8nv`.

## Future Follow-up Trigger
After `haxe.go` selective runtime + metal fallback implementation stabilizes, run a new GPT-5.2 Pro cross-repo spike (Go/Rust/Elixir/hxhx) and reconcile family spec.

title: Replace Stage3 backend reflective emit fallback with typed dispatch
description:
Problem
- `packages/hxhx/src/hxhx/Stage3Compiler.hx` still has a reflective fallback in `emitWithBackend`:
  - `Reflect.field(backendReflect, "emit")`
  - `Reflect.callMethod(...)`
- This seam is currently justified as a bootstrap compatibility boundary, but it keeps `Dynamic`/reflection on a correctness-critical path and weakens static guarantees.

Goal
- Remove (or strictly eliminate in default paths) the reflective backend emit fallback by moving to typed backend dispatch contracts for dynamic/bundled providers.

Scope
1) Define typed fallback contract for backend emit dispatch that works in Stage3 bootstrap lane.
2) Replace reflective emit lookup/invoke in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend` with typed dispatch through boundary helpers.
3) Keep compatibility with existing builtin backends and dynamic provider loading semantics.
4) Keep any unavoidable boundary cast isolated in one helper with guardrails.
5) Add/update tests and docs for dispatch policy.

Acceptance criteria
- No `Reflect.callMethod` remains in `Stage3Compiler.emitWithBackend`.
- Builtin target flows (`ocaml-stage3`, `js-native`) remain green.
- Dynamic/bundled provider path still loads and emits successfully in integration tests.
- `ci:guards` + backend wiring/provider tests pass.
- Docs clearly state allowed dispatch boundaries (if any remain).
acceptance_criteria: No Reflect.callMethod in Stage3 emit path; typed dispatch preserved for builtin + dynamic provider backends; tests and guardrails green.

- Is wrapper selection expected for bootstrap regen lanes, or should we default to native stage0 Haxe for deterministic resource/latency behavior?

Scope:
1) Reproduce benchmarked comparison (wrapper vs native binary) with report artifacts.
2) Decide bootstrap-stage0 binary selection policy and make default explicit.
3) Implement guardrails (warning/fail-fast/doc guidance) when wrapper binary is detected in critical regen lanes.

- Added `--stage0-selection-only` mode for no-emit selection probes (writes report and exits).

title: Stage0 memory/perf hardening (Full1 perf credibility blocker)
description:
Short failfast probes (65s, heartbeat=20s) still show >6GB stage0 emitter RSS in both policy lanes, so wrapper-vs-native selection alone is not sufficient.

Repro commands:
1) Wrapper policy
   HAXE_BIN="$(which haxe)" HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_STAGE0_HAXE_POLICY=warn HXHX_STAGE0_HEARTBEAT=20 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=65 \
   bash scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh --incremental --no-verify --force --report-json .tmp/stage0-wrapper-failfast.json
2) Native policy
   HAXE_BIN="$(which haxe)" HXHX_BOOTSTRAP_STAGE0_HAXE_POLICY=prefer-native HXHX_STAGE0_HEARTBEAT=20 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=65 \
   bash scripts/hxhx/regenerate-hxhx-bootstrap.sh --incremental --no-verify --force --report-json .tmp/stage0-native-failfast.json

Observed peaks (from report JSON):
- wrapper: stage0_observability.heartbeat_peak_rss_mb=6818
- native: stage0_observability.heartbeat_peak_rss_mb=6643

Hypothesis:
- Primary memory pressure is likely inside stage0 compilation workload (emit path / graph size / macro expansion), not wrapper-process overhead.
- Native selection is still required for determinism and slight improvement, but deeper optimization needs targeted profiling.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Add reproducible profiling workflow that identifies top stage0 memory contributors in regen lane (module/pass or compiler options).\n2) Land at least one mitigation that materially reduces peak RSS (target >=20% reduction on the same failfast probe and/or full run evidence).\n3) Document validated knobs and expected envelope in STAGE0_POLICY/TESTING docs, with before-vs-after report JSON evidence.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Follow-up variance sweep (2026-03-03): OCAMLRUNPARAM candidate comparison

Method:
- same failfast profile probe for all runs (policy=prefer-native, failfast=65, heartbeat=20, no_opt=0, no_inline=0, disable_prepasses=0)
- 3 runs each for unset, s=2M, s=4M; 1 run for s=8M

Aggregated results (peak_rss_mb):
- unset (n=3): 6172, 6007, 6216
  - avg=6131.67, median=6172
- s=2M (n=3): 4873, 5549, 5299
  - avg=5240.33, median=5299
  - reduction vs unset: avg=14.54%, median=14.14%
- s=4M (n=3): 5012, 4843, 5379
  - avg=5078.00, median=5012
  - reduction vs unset: avg=17.18%, median=18.79%
- s=8M (n=1): 5353
  - reduction vs unset single-sample: avg=12.70%

Interpretation:
- improvement is real but variable; this run family does NOT show stable >=20% reduction on 3-run aggregates.
- among current candidates, s=4M has the strongest aggregate profile; s=2M produced the best single outlier (4873) but weaker aggregate.

Recommendation:
- keep OCAMLRUNPARAM tuning opt-in for now (do not set global default yet).
- next step: longer/full regen comparison for unset vs s=4M to decide whether CI lane default is justified.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Session 2026-03-04 evidence (post direct-flag/bootstrap parity work):

Repeated full regen runs (prefer-native policy, heartbeat=20s) show large variance in stage0 emit RSS envelope.

Representative runs:
- High-spike run: peak 10022MB at 80s, total emit 891s (verify pass)
- Mid run: peak ~9104MB at 100s, total emit 858s (verify failed due unrelated type mismatch fixed later)
- Native-low runs after resolver/path stabilization: sustained 1.0-3.8GB windows for long stretches, with occasional 4-6GB spikes; e.g. run with extended failfast reached as low as 998MB at 300s and 1087MB at 260s on another run.

Important takeaway: native stage0 path can materially reduce memory in many windows, but peak behavior remains highly variable and can still spike to multi-GB levels depending on compile phase/timing. This task remains valid as a root-cause/perf-hardening backlog item even after native path cutover.

title: Bootstrap/source build throughput: native stage0 default + configurable dune workers
description:
Context from 2026-03-04 sessions:
- Running stage0/source lane through the Lix shim (which haxe -> ~/.nvm/.../lix/bin/haxeshim.js) showed severe memory/time behavior (multiple GB spikes; long tail builds).
- Switching to native Haxe binary (/Users/fullofcaffeine/haxe/versions/4.3.7/haxe) immediately improved early heartbeat RSS (roughly from ~7GB windows to ~1.2GB windows in comparable probes) and smoother progress.
- Build path in focus: scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh (source lane with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1) and bootstrap compile via dune.

Problem statement:
Even with native stage0 selection policy work underway, developer UX is still poor for full source rebuilds and CI reruns. We need deterministic, documented throughput controls (especially worker parallelism) and benchmark evidence for safe defaults on local + CI environments.

Scope:
1) Add explicit, documented worker controls for relevant build steps:
   - stage0 Haxe source build lane (where applicable)
   - dune bootstrap build lane (out.bc/out.exe)
2) Benchmark matrix for representative settings:
   - native-vs-wrapper stage0 binary
   - worker counts (e.g., auto, 1, 2, 4, 8)
   - collect wall time + peak RSS from existing heartbeat/report telemetry
3) Choose safe default(s) and expose override knobs in scripts/docs.
4) Ensure CI reproducibility: same knobs available in workflow env with clear marker output.
acceptance_criteria:
1) build-hxhx lane supports deterministic worker configuration via env/flag (documented in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh help/docs).
2) A benchmark artifact/table is produced for at least one local run and one CI-like run, showing time + peak RSS across worker settings and stage0 binary modes.
3) Selected default setting is justified in docs (STAGE0_POLICY + TESTING + README quick note), including when to override.
4) CI logs include resolved stage0 binary path and effective worker configuration for auditable runs.
5) No behavioral regressions: npm run -s ci:guards passes and gate scripts still execute with default knobs.
close_reason: Implemented worker matrix controls, benchmark artifact table (local + CI-like), docs default/override guidance, and guard validation.

title: Stage0 --connect handoff hang after source emit (client waits while server idle)
description: During source builds with repo server reuse (HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER=1), the stage0 run can finish generation and populate packages/hxhx/out/**, but the `haxe build.hxml -D ocaml_build=byte --connect <port>` client remains blocked indefinitely. In one run, both client and server dropped to near-idle while the build script kept waiting, requiring manual kill and a direct `dune build ./out.bc` continuation. This creates long false hangs and hides successful progress.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Repro command is deterministic and documented (build-hxhx source lane with --connect). 2) Build script detects stalled or idle --connect handoff and fails fast with actionable message OR auto-recovers by switching to direct non-connect stage0 invocation. 3) On success, script always exits with produced out.bc/out.exe path and no manual kill needed. 4) Add regression coverage (scripted smoke) and doc guidance for when to disable HXHX_STAGE0_USE_REPO_SERVER.
notes: Implemented connect-handoff auto-recovery in scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh: if --connect lane is idle (no log growth + idle process tree) for HXHX_STAGE0_CONNECT_IDLE_SECS, kill stalled client and retry once without --connect. Added deterministic regression smoke scripts/hxhx/test-build-hxhx-connect-retry.sh (npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke), wired into .github/workflows/ci.yml guards job, and documented knob in README.md + docs/01-getting-started/TESTING.md. Local validation: npm run test:hxhx:build-connect-retry-smoke, npm run ci:guards, npm run test:hxhx:cli-contract.
close_reason: Implemented connect stall detector + auto-retry without --connect, added CI smoke coverage, and documented operator knobs.

title: Stage0 RSS source-level mitigation beyond runtime flags
description:
Repeated A/B probes with current runtime/build knobs do not yield stable >=20% median RSS reduction in failfast windows (90s/120s). We need source-level mitigation work targeting dominant compiler contributors rather than more flag sweeps.

Latest evidence:
- disable-prepasses (120s, reps=3): median reduction ~4.19%
- no-opt+disable-prepasses (120s, reps=3): median reduction ~3.10%
- disable-prepasses+s=2M (120s, reps=3): median regression ~-17.97%
- disable-prepasses (90s, reps=3): median reduction ~1.94%

Scope:
1) Identify a concrete source-level mitigation candidate (e.g., reducing retained AST/metadata in hot phases, staged emit partitioning, or pass-level memory reclamation points) with explicit rationale.
2) Implement the mitigation behind a deterministic toggle for A/B verification.
3) Validate with repeated A/B runner (reps>=3) and report median reduction on 120s failfast probes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Mitigation implementation lands with docs on what it changes and why.\n2) Repeated A/B evidence (120s failfast, reps>=3) is attached as artifacts with summary.json.\n3) Either achieves >=20% median reduction OR documents why not and proposes next measurable mitigation with residual-risk note.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07 xhigh follow-up: reviewed remaining runtime macro gaps against actual repo call sites. The next materially missing seam is not another Context getter; it is richer runtime Type fidelity. In particular, runtime TypeTools.applyTypeParameters() is still identity-only and TypeTools.iter() is still effectively a no-op for the synthetic external-host model, while real reflaxe.ocaml compiler code uses applyTypeParameters() heavily on TType/TAbstract paths. Closing bxlg.9.5 before either (a) widening the runtime Type model enough to make those semantics honest, or (b) explicitly scoping them out of Full1, would be misleading. Recommendation: stop adding convenience rungs and treat the next step as either a deliberate richer-Type-model slice or a scope decision under bxlg.9.6/f1cl.4.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07: landed the next honest runtime Type fidelity slice. External-host runtime TypeTools.applyTypeParameters() now performs recursive substitution through the current synthetic Type model, TypeTools.iter() now traverses direct children instead of no-oping, and follow(TType(...)) now substitutes typedef payload params. Validation is through the external-host macro probe rather than direct Type pattern-matching, because generated OCaml still cannot safely reconstruct or destructure synthetic TAbstract wrappers without hitting the upstream constructor-name collision in haxe.macro.Type / ModuleType. Remaining fidelity gap is therefore narrower and explicit: synthetic abstract-wrapper preservation and richer typed/module metadata are still below Full1 expectations.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: 2026-03-07 xhigh sufficiency review: still not closable. The latest runtime Type slice removes the worst lie (applyTypeParameters is no longer identity-only, iter is no longer a no-op, and follow(TType(...)) now substitutes typedef payload params), which is enough for the current reflaxe.ocaml typedef-heavy call sites and the external-host probe. But it is still below an honest Full1 macro API parity claim. Two semantic seams remain material: (1) synthetic abstract-wrapper fidelity is still missing, so followWithAbstracts/applyTypeParameters over abstract-heavy paths still collapse to underlying types instead of preserving a real abstract wrapper; (2) synthetic module/type metadata is still narrower than upstream because enum/typedef/abstract declaration kinds still round-trip as class-shaped refs in external-host mode. This matters beyond synthetic probes: vendored reflaxe.elixir code exercises applyTypeParameters + followWithAbstracts over typedef/abstract-rich flows. Recommendation: do not move to bxlg.9.6 yet. The next acceptable step is a deliberate xhigh slice for synthetic abstract-wrapper fidelity and richer declaration-kind/module metadata, or an explicit Full1 scope decision that those semantics are out of scope.

title: Narrow Dynamic usage in provider resolver helper
description:
Problem
- `BackendProviderResolver.requireProvider` still accepts `instance:Dynamic` even though the only behavior needed there is validating the `ITargetBackendProvider` contract and bridging to structural dispatch.
- The project rule forbids broad `Dynamic` usage except where narrowly justified at runtime boundaries.

Goal
- Reduce `Dynamic` scope in provider resolution by narrowing helper signatures to typed contracts while preserving current behavior.

Scope
1) Change `requireProvider` to accept a typed contract (`Null<ITargetBackendProvider>`) instead of `Dynamic`.
2) Keep constructor error handling unchanged in `registrationsForType`.
3) Keep the one scoped boundary cast (`return cast providerContract`) unchanged for now.
4) Update docs/comments only if behavior/contract wording changes.

Acceptance criteria
- `BackendProviderResolver` no longer takes `Dynamic` in `requireProvider`.
- Provider resolver integration tests remain green.
- `ci:guards` remains green (including provider boundary guard).
close_reason: Narrowed provider helper typing; dynamic boundary now downcast immediately in resolver path.

title: Fix stage0 source-build failure in HxParser optional-branch lowering
description: Stage0 Source Smoke run 22212268257 progressed past prior OOM kill and now fails deterministically during dune build with an OCaml type error in generated HxParser.ml. Failing expression currently emits: let elseBranch = Obj.obj (HxEnum.unbox_or_obj "HxStmt" (if acceptKeyword ... then parseStmt ... else Obj.magic (HxRuntime.hx_null))). This indicates the optional branch conversion path is mixing Obj.t/hxenum conversions incorrectly for nullable stmt branches in stage0-generated output.

title: Gate1: expression macro expansion rung
description: Upstream Gate1 uses expression macros heavily (e.g. unit.HelperMacros.getCompilationDate()) in normal code. A real compiler must execute these macros at compile time and splice the resulting AST.\n\nImplement an initial expression-macro expansion rung that can execute a small, allowlisted set of macro entrypoints (likely via the existing Stage4 macro host) and replace call sites with returned expressions.
design:
Start minimal:
- Only support calls shaped like pack.Class.meth() and pack.Class.meth(<string literal>)
- Macro host returns a serialized Expr (new protocol message) or a small textual subset that we parse into HxExpr
- Expansion occurs before typing
- Clean-room implementation: upstream is oracle-only via untracked vendor checkout
acceptance_criteria: - Can compile upstream-ish macro call sites like HelperMacros.getCompilationDate() when allowlisted\n- Limitations are documented; expansion is auditable (exact entrypoint strings)\n- Keep npm test green
notes: Implemented expression macro expansion rung: new macro.expandExpr RPC, ExprMacroExpander pre-typing pass (HXHX_EXPR_MACROS allowlist), macro host entrypoint registry returns String for string-returning macros; added ExprMacroShim + Stage3 test rung; fixed OCaml string escaping + avoided nullable-enum boxing in expander. Quality gates: npm run ci:guards + npm test pass.

title: js-native: support break/continue loop control markers
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently represents `break;` and `continue;` as `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"|"continue"), ...)`.
- js-native emit currently treats all `EUnsupported(...)` as hard errors, so loop-control statements fail even in simple loop code.

Scope
1) Add explicit js-native lowering for statement-level `EUnsupported("break")` and `EUnsupported("continue")`.
2) Keep behavior narrow: only statement positions should lower to JS loop-control keywords.
3) Do not broaden unsupported-expression semantics globally; preserve fail-fast behavior for other unsupported expression kinds.
4) Add target smoke coverage for break/continue in loop bodies.

Constraints
- Keep non-js backends unchanged.
- No `Any`; avoid new `Dynamic` usage.
- Keep implementation small and easy to remove once parser gains structured `SBreak`/`SContinue` nodes.
acceptance_criteria:
- js-native can emit+run a fixture using `break` and `continue` inside loops.
- Existing js-native and Stage3 target tests remain green.
- Unsupported expression handling still fails fast for non-whitelisted raw markers.
notes:
Implemented narrow js-native lowering for loop-control markers emitted by native parser:
- `JsStmtEmitter` now maps `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"), ...)` to `break;`
- `JsStmtEmitter` now maps `SExpr(EUnsupported("continue"), ...)` to `continue;`
- other unsupported expression kinds remain fail-fast.

Added smoke fixture `JsNativeLoopControlMain` to `scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh` validating while+break+continue output (`js-native-loop-control:5:8`).

Validation:
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh`
- `HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets`
All green.
close_reason: js-native loop-control markers supported and covered by full target suite.

title: hih AST: make break/continue first-class statements
description:
Problem
- Native parser currently lowers `break;` and `continue;` as `SExpr(EUnsupported("break"|"continue"), ...)`.
- js-native currently has a marker-specific workaround in statement emission.
- This keeps loop control out of the typed statement model and makes semantics indirect.

Goal
- Promote loop control to first-class statement nodes in the Stage3 AST.
- Keep js-native semantics explicit and remove dependency on unsupported-expression markers for normal control flow.

Scope
1) Add statement nodes for break/continue in `HxStmt`.
2) Parse `break` and `continue` into those nodes in native parser.
3) Update typer traversal / macro stmt rewriting / unsupported counters for new nodes.
4) Update js-native stmt emitter to lower new nodes directly.
5) Update OCaml Stage3 stmt handling to compile safely with the new nodes (no pattern-match gaps).
6) Remove now-redundant js-native marker special-casing for break/continue.

Constraints
- Keep this change narrow and behavior-preserving for existing tests.
- Do not use `Any`; avoid new `Dynamic` unless strictly boundary-related.
- Preserve fail-fast for truly unsupported expression forms.
acceptance_criteria:
- Native parser no longer emits `EUnsupported("break")` / `EUnsupported("continue")` for statement-level loop control.
- js-native loop-control smoke still passes.
- Full `npm run -s test:hxhx-targets` passes.
- No remaining js-native statement-emitter dependence on unsupported break/continue markers.
notes:
Implemented first-class statement nodes for loop control in the HIH AST.

Changes
- Added `SBreak(pos)` and `SContinue(pos)` to `HxStmt`.
- Native parser now lowers `break;` / `continue;` to these nodes (instead of `SExpr(EUnsupported(...))`).
- Updated statement traversal sites:
  - typer (`TyperStage`)
  - macro statement rewriter (`ExprMacroExpander`)
  - Stage3 unsupported counters (`Stage3Compiler`)
  - function return scanning (`HxFunctionDecl`)
- js-native emitter now lowers `SBreak`/`SContinue` directly and no longer depends on unsupported-marker pattern matching.
- OCaml Stage3 emitter now handles `SBreak`/`SContinue` in statement lowering and dependency-walk switches so builds remain total.

Validation
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=3600 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh`
- `HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets`
All green; js-native loop-control and do/while smoke lanes pass.
close_reason: break/continue promoted to first-class statements and validated across Stage3/js-native flows.

title: backend boundary follow-up: centralize GenIrProgram recovery cast helper
description:
Context
- We currently use `requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram { return cast program; }` in:
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/js/JsTargetCore.hx`
  - `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/ocaml/OcamlTargetCore.hx`
- This cast is currently justified because reflaxe/OCaml dispatch can degrade `ITargetCore.emit` parameters to `Obj.t` at generated OCaml interface boundaries.
- Without boundary recovery, Stage0 build fails in generated ML with type mismatch:
  - `program has type Obj.t but expected MacroExpandedProgram.t`.

Problem
- The cast is correct today, but duplicated in multiple target cores.
- Duplicated boundary recovery logic increases drift risk and obscures where dynamic recovery is allowed.
- We need one canonical, documented boundary policy that survives backend growth (js/ocaml and future promoted targets).

Goal
- Centralize `GenIrProgram` boundary recovery in one shared helper/pattern.
- Keep target-core emitters fully typed and free of ad-hoc boundary casts.
- Preserve current behavior and Stage0 build stability.

Scope
1) Design a shared helper for boundary recovery (single location, minimal surface).
2) Migrate `JsTargetCore` and `OcamlTargetCore` to the shared helper.
3) Define explicit policy for where boundary casts are allowed vs forbidden.
4) Add a targeted regression check that would fail if boundary recovery is removed or drifted.
5) Document the final pattern in backend architecture docs.

Proposed Implementation (candidate)
- Add one utility under backend layer, e.g. `packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx`:
  - `public static inline function requireProgram(program:GenIrProgram):GenIrProgram`.
- Replace local `requireProgram(...)` duplicates in target cores with helper call.
- Keep any unavoidable casts at Stage3 reflection/provider seams explicitly documented.

Constraints
- No upstream code copying; keep MIT clean-room workflow.
- No behavior change in backend output.
- Keep changes minimal and reviewable.

Risk/Tradeoffs
- Over-aggressive refactor could destabilize Stage3 bootstrap.
- Keeping duplicates invites divergence when additional target cores land.

Validation
- `haxe -cp packages/hxhx/src -cp packages/hih-compiler/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/src -cp packages/reflaxe.ocaml/std -main hxhx.Main --no-output -D hih_native_parser`
- `npm run -s test:hxhx:builtin-target-smoke`
- If available in same session: a Stage0 bootstrap build proving no `Obj.t` vs `MacroExpandedProgram.t` regression in generated ML.

Notes
- This is follow-up technical debt after boundary hardening work in `haxe.ocaml-3b7`.
- Priority intentionally set to later (not blocker) because current casts are correct and localized.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A shared backend boundary helper exists and is used by both JsTargetCore and OcamlTargetCore instead of duplicated local requireProgram helpers. 2) Cast policy is documented: allowed only at explicit boundary seams; forbidden in core emitter logic. 3) Compile + smoke validation pass (native parser no-output + builtin target smoke). 4) At least one bootstrap/generated-ML validation note is recorded showing no Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram.t regression.
notes: Implemented central boundary helper packages/hih-compiler/src/backend/GenIrBoundary.hx and migrated JsTargetCore/OcamlTargetCore to it. Added explicit Stage3 backend-dispatch seam handling so reflaxe OCaml output no longer regresses Obj.t vs MacroExpandedProgram at the emit bridge boundary (validated with HXHX_FORCE_STAGE0=1 HXHX_STAGE0_FAILFAST_SECS=1200 bash scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh). Also validated native parser compile smoke and full target workflow (HXHX_BIN=packages/hxhx/out/_build/default/out.bc npm run -s test:hxhx-targets).

title: Fix nullable Bytes method lowering in haxe.http.HttpBase
description:
Strict portable compilation fails when `haxe.http.HttpBase` is included because nullable-Bytes method lowering falls back to a unit placeholder.

Observed failure in generated `haxe_http_HttpBase.ml`:
- `responseAsString <- (() : string)`

Expected:
- `responseBytes.toString()` should lower to `HxBytes.toString ...` (or equivalent) and never emit unit placeholder in a `string`-typed assignment.

Reproducer:
- Compile fixture `test/portable/fixtures/haxe_http_bucket01_basic` with:
  - `-D ocaml_build=native`
  - `-D ocaml_portable_native_surface=error`
acceptance_criteria: - haxe_http_bucket01_basic compiles and runs in strict portable lane\n- Generated HttpBase getter no longer emits unit placeholder for string assignment\n- Existing bytes/runtime tests remain green
close_reason: Supported UTF8/RawNative/default Bytes encodings in lowering and added regression test for HttpBase responseData nullable-Bytes path

title: HXHX Stage 2: non-shim compiler bring-up

title: hxhx: stage1 --no-output compile (module resolution + parse)
description: Add a stage1 execution path in the hxhx binary that can handle a minimal Haxe project without delegating to stage0: resolve -cp/-main, load the main module, parse it via the frontend seam.
design:
- New shim-only flag: --hxhx-stage1 (never forwarded to stage0)
- Implement minimal CLI arg handling for: -cp, -main, --no-output
- Implement module resolution: find <Main>.hx in classpath; validate package matches
- Parse via ParserStage (native frontend when enabled).
- Keep behavior conservative: if unsupported flags appear, print a clear error and exit nonzero.
acceptance_criteria: - New command works: hxhx --hxhx-stage1 -cp <dir> -main Main --no-output\n- Unit/acceptance test covers it\n- Existing stage0 shim tests still pass

title: hxhx stage1: resolve -cp paths relative to .hxml

title: hxhx stage1: support -C/--cwd

- Stage1 accepts -C/--cwd
- Relative -cp values resolve against cwd

title: hxhx stage1: accept long-form flag aliases

acceptance_criteria: - Stage1 accepts --class-path/--main/--library\n- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh uses at least one long-form alias\n- npm test passes

title: hxhx stage1: support --std classpath
description: Add --std <dir> support in Stage1Args, and treat it as an additional classpath root for module resolution. This is the minimal step toward resolving Haxe stdlib modules (haxe.*, sys.*, etc.) in non-shim mode.

title: hxhx stage1: infer std path from env

title: Control flow: return inside if/loops should work
description:
Patterns like `if (cond) return v;` currently lower to OCaml expressions that do not actually return, because `TReturn` is treated as an expression and `if` without `else` is forced to unit.

Implement a strategy for early returns inside expression positions (e.g. rewrite function body to CPS, or raise a private return exception caught at function boundary).

This is required for idiomatic Haxe code and for larger bootstrapping workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
- `if (cond) return v;` behaves correctly (no fallthrough)
- Works inside loops (e.g. inside `while` body)
- Add a regression test (compile → dune build → run)

This is a parity blocker for behavior-level evidence beyond compile/constructor coverage.

- Add minimal reproducer fixture assertions for BufferInput.readByte and typed array element reads
- Fix runtime/backend lowering so fixture runs without crash and values match expected semantics
- Keep strict portable lane compile/run green for haxe.io bucket fixtures
notes: Additional repro during haxe.io-02 closure: UInt8Array.fromArray currently crashes at runtime (Invalid_argument("Char.chr") via HxBytes.set). Bucket fixture uses fromBytes/sub/subarray constructor coverage until runtime correctness is fixed.

title: [bug] runtime haxe.rtti usage fails in OCaml emit lane
description:
Portable fixture attempts to execute runtime haxe.rtti paths currently fail during dune compile in OCaml output. Repros observed while implementing haxe.rtti closure bucket:

1) Using CType enum constructor in runtime code generated an Obj.t mismatch in Main.ml (string constant emitted where Obj.t expected).

Reference: upstream Haxe typed AST dump for Null<Int> shows: if (tmp != null) tmp else 2 has overall type Int, then-branch type Null<Int>.

title: Codegen: support ++/-- on instance fields
description:
We currently drop OpIncrement/OpDecrement when the operand is not a ref-local (e.g. `self.i++`), which can cause infinite loops in generated OCaml (e.g. lexers).

Implement `++/--` lowering for:
- instance var fields (`TField(_, FInstance(...))`)
- static vars
- array elements (`TArray`) where feasible

Prefer correct statement semantics first; document expression-value nuances (prefix/postfix) for later.

title: hih native frontend: extend protocol to carry statement bodies
description: Protocol v1 only transmits method summaries (signature + first-return hints), which prevents Stage3 from emitting full OCaml bodies when using the native frontend.\n\nWe currently work around this for bring-up via HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER=1 (pure-Haxe parser) when --hxhx-emit-full-bodies is enabled, but that won't scale to upstream modules that the pure parser cannot yet parse.
design: Add a backward-compatible protocol extension (prefer bumping to v=2) that can transmit a minimal statement AST for function bodies. Keep the subset aligned with HxStmt/HxExpr (SBlock/SVar/SIf/SExpr/SReturn/SReturnVoid + basic Expr forms like call/field/binop/unop/literals/ident).\n\nDecoding should be best-effort: unknown stmt/expr forms map to EUnsupported so the pipeline can keep progressing.
acceptance_criteria: - Native parser can emit bodies for the minimal subset (at least SExpr(trace("HELLO");)).\n- ParserStage decoder rehydrates bodies into HxFunctionDecl.body.\n- Stage3 --hxhx-emit-full-bodies no longer needs HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER for the subset (add a regression test).

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
Implemented native frontend method body transport for Stage3 full-body emission.

- packages/hih-compiler/src/EmitterStage.hx now only treats locals as emit-safe when emitFullBodies=true (avoids unbound locals in return-only mode).
- Stage3 no longer auto-forces HIH_FORCE_HX_PARSER for --hxhx-emit-full-bodies; native protocol supplies bodies for the minimal subset.

title: Stage4: remove stage0 dependency for building hxhx-macro-host
description: Gate1/Gate2 runners currently auto-build the macro host by invoking stage0 'haxe' via scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx-macro-host.sh when HXHX_MACRO_HOST_EXE is unset. design:
Options (pick one):
1) Ship prebuilt macro-host binaries as release artifacts and have runners download/cache them (preferred for CI, but OS-specific).
2) Build macro host via hxhx Stage3 emitter + dune (requires Stage3 emitter to handle macro-host code subset).
3) Replace macro host with a minimal OCaml-only host for early rungs, keeping protocol the same.
acceptance_criteria: - Running npm scripts that invoke Stage4 macro execution does not need stage0 haxe to *build* or *select* a macro host\n- CI/Gate runners document expected macro-host provenance (prebuilt vs built)\n- Keep npm test green

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
2026-02-11 progress: added stage3_emit_runner timeout/heartbeat diagnostics and narrowed the current stall point.

Landed diagnostics
- New env knobs in scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-runci-macro.sh:
  - HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 600, 0 disables timeout)
  - HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_HEARTBEAT_SEC (default 20, 0 disables heartbeat)
- Heartbeat now reports subinvocation count + last wrapped command.
- haxelib wrapper now also logs invocations to the same wrap log as haxe.

Current blocker observed
- In HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner, run frequently times out after RunCi returns from echoServer build:
  - last wrapped command remains "haxe build.hxml"
  - no subsequent Macro-stage subcommands are issued before timeout.
- This indicates control-flow/runtime semantics issue after early RunCi setup rather than simple wrapper/logging blindness.

Repro
- HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_TIMEOUT_SEC=45 HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_HEARTBEAT_SEC=10 bash scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-runci-macro.sh

Next
- inspect generated RunCi runtime path around test-loop entry (post-echoServer) and isolate the semantic mismatch causing the stall.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text:
2026-02-11 progress: fixed Stage3 `sys.io.Process` semantics so Gate2 `stage3_emit_runner` moves past early RunCi bootstrap stalls.

What landed
- `packages/hih-compiler/src/EmitterStage.hx`
  - `new sys.io.Process(cmd,args[,detached])` lowers to `HxBootProcess.spawn` (async) instead of `run`.
  - Added lowering for `process.kill()` -> `HxBootProcess.kill`.
  - Relaxed `process.exitCode(...)` matcher to accept 0 or 1 arg forms.
- `packages/hih-compiler/shims/HxBootProcess.ml`
  - Reworked shim to real async process lifecycle (`spawn`, `waitpid`, buffered stdout/stderr, `kill`, deterministic `close`).
- `scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh`
  - Added Stage3 regression asserting constructor lowers to `HxBootProcess.spawn` and `kill()` lowers correctly.
- Regenerated bootstrap snapshot: `packages/hxhx/bootstrap_out/EmitterStage.ml`.

Validation
- `npm run -s test:hxhx-targets` -> OK (includes new regression).
- `HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_TIMEOUT_SEC=45 HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_HEARTBEAT_SEC=10 bash scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-runci-macro.sh`
  - no longer stalls immediately after echoServer; now progresses deep into RunCi before timeout.
- `HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_TIMEOUT_SEC=240 HXHX_GATE2_RUNCI_HEARTBEAT_SEC=20 bash scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-runci-macro.sh`
  - `run=ok`, `subinvocations=23`.
- `npm run -s test:upstream:runci-macro-stage3-display` -> OK.

Note
- The stage3_emit_runner path still emits many OCaml warning-20 notices from generated macro bridge stubs; functional run is green.

title: Gate2 stage3_emit_runner: fix field-access precedence on call results
description: Non-delegating Gate2 stage3_emit_runner currently fails while compiling upstream runci/System.hx mergeArgs. Generated OCaml in Runci_System.ml emits Obj.repr <call> without parenthesizing the call expression when lowering field access on call results, causing over-application errors (Obj.repr applied to too many arguments).
acceptance_criteria:
- Add a regression that exercises call-result field access with chained array operations (concat/map/join)-style lowering
- Stage3 emitted OCaml compiles for that regression (no Obj.repr over-application)
- HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner progresses past this compile failure (no Runci_System.ml Obj.repr arity error)
- npm run test:hxhx-targets remains green
close_reason: Validated locally with test:hxhx-targets, test:upstream:runci-macro(stage3_emit_runner), and ci:guards; regressions added for call-result precedence and callback binding.

title: Reduce bootstrap snapshot size to avoid >50MB GitHub warning

acceptance_criteria: - git push to origin/main has no >50MB warning for bootstrap snapshot files\n- Stage0-free build path still works from committed bootstrap_out\n- test:hxhx-targets and ci:guards remain green

- HXHX_GATE2_MODE=stage3_emit_runner npm run test:upstream:runci-macro runs upstream tests/RunCi.hxml unmodified

title: Gate2: restore build-hxhx stdout path contract after bootstrap hydration
description: After introducing bootstrap shard hydration, scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh now emits hydration status on stdout. Gate2 wrappers that capture HXHX_BIN via command substitution expect stdout to contain only the executable path, so the run fails with an invalid binary path. Restore the stdout contract (path only) and add a regression check.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx.sh writes only the executable path to stdout in the success path
- Gate2 runner scripts that capture HXHX_BIN via command substitution work again
- Add regression coverage in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh for the build-hxhx stdout contract
- npm run -s test:hxhx-targets and npm run -s test:upstream:runci-macro pass
close_reason: Restored build-hxhx stdout path contract by moving hydration/build chatter to stderr, hardened upstream runner scripts to parse build-hxhx output via tail -n 1, and added regression coverage in test:hxhx-targets to fail if build-hxhx stdout contains more than one line. Validated with npm run -s ci:guards, npm run -s test:hxhx-targets, and HXHX_GATE2_MACRO_STOP_AFTER=display npm run -s test:upstream:runci-macro. Full Gate2 direct run still hits a separate segfault tracked in haxe.ocaml-xgv.10.22.

title: Gate2 stage3_no_emit_direct: investigate segfault in tests/misc/resolution run.hxml

acceptance_criteria: - Reproduce segfault with explicit stage markers and captured last wrapped invocation\n- Either fix the crash or add a deterministic host-gated skip with documented reason\n- Gate2 direct runner reports stable outcome (pass or explicit skip) instead of segfault

- Workflow exports HXHX_GATE3_TARGETS from dispatch input and prints a per-target summary in logs

title: Gate1: module-local helper types (multi-class modules)
description:
Upstream Gate1 (tests/unit/compile-macro.hxml) includes many modules that declare helper types in the same .hx file (for example: private class CastHelper inside TestNumericCasts.hx). Today the Stage3 pipeline models only the module's main class, so OCaml emission fails with errors like: Unbound module CastHelper.

Implement enough of Haxe's multi-type module semantics for Gate1 bring-up:
- Discover additional class declarations in a module (at least names and static vars/constants).
- Preserve them on the Haxe side (HxModuleDecl must expose all classes in the module).
- Make Stage3 emission generate OCaml providers for those helper types (stubs are fine in bring-up, but they must define referenced static vars/constants).

Clean-room requirement: do not copy upstream compiler or tests into this repo; upstream is an untracked behavior oracle only.

title: Stage3: investigate intermittent exit 139 during full display emit
description: Observed intermittent process exit 139 when running stage3 full-body display emit on vendor/haxe/tests/display/build.hxml. Capture repro frequency and root cause; add deterministic regression if feasible.

comments.author: Marcelo Serpa
comments.text: Root cause: warm --hxhx-out full-emit reruns could pass a reduced OCaml unit list to ocamlopt (modules present on disk from prior run but omitted from current argv), causing intermittent link errors/segfault-shaped failures. Fix: EmitterStage now folds existing canonicalized .ml units in out/ into the compile candidate set (excluding legacy out.ml), then de-duplicates case-insensitively before ocamldep sort/ocamlopt. Added dedicated stress regression: scripts/hxhx/run-upstream-display-stage3-emit-stress.sh (new npm script test:upstream:display-stage3-emit-stress) with per-iteration progress and warm out-dir reuse. description: Add a native macro execution model to hxhx so macros (and compiler plugins) run inside the hxhx binary rather than being delegated to stage0. This unlocks true self-hosting and later builtin-backend linking (yvp.5).

- hxhx can execute a minimal macro (Context.getType + generate code) without stage0
- Compiler plugin hooks work (load + run) for at least one backend

title: hxhx(stage3): use ocamldep -sort for multi-module build order
description: Stage3 multi-module emit currently passes .ml units to ocamlopt in resolver order, which can put providers (Std, Sys, etc) after users and fail with OCaml error "Unbound module X". Run ocamldep -sort on emitted units to compute a dependency-respecting order, then link with the root module last to preserve main init ordering.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up no longer fails with "Unbound module Std" due to unit ordering (next failure should be later)
close_reason: Stage3 build uses ocamldep -sort and emits a tiny Std shim; upstream compile-macro bring-up progresses past Unbound module Std (next failure: untyped)

title: hxhx(stage3): lex untyped/cast to avoid emitting bogus identifiers
description: Upstream-ish std code uses `untyped` (and sometimes `cast`) in return expressions. Stage3 lexer currently tokenizes these as identifiers, so emission can produce OCaml names like `untyped` and fail with Unbound value. Recognize them as keywords so the parser marks them unsupported and the Stage3 emitter collapses the whole return expression to Obj.magic.
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up no longer fails with Unbound value untyped
notes: Close note: Stage3 lexer now treats "untyped" and "cast" as keywords so return-expr parsing collapses those expressions instead of emitting an OCaml identifier named untyped.
close_reason: Lexer recognizes untyped/cast as keywords so Stage3 doesn't emit bogus  identifiers (upstream compile-macro now fails later)

title: hxhx(stage3): collapse return exprs that reference unknown value identifiers
description: Stage3 emitter currently attempts to emit return expressions that reference locals/fields/helpers (e.g. `b`, `tryNewBytes`, `untyped__...`) even though Stage3 does not model class fields or locals. This produces OCaml with unbound values. Treat any lowercase identifier in a return expression as poison unless it is a function parameter, and collapse such return expressions to the bring-up escape hatch (Obj.magic 0).
acceptance_criteria:
- scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh passes
- Stage3 upstream compile-macro bring-up progresses past Bytes.ml unbound values like trynewBytes (next failure should be later)
close_reason: Stage3 now collapses return exprs that reference non-param value idents; upstream compile-macro bring-up emits/builds/runs successfully (still non-semantic).

title: hxhx(stage4): bundle macro host in dist + auto-discover
description: Improve Stage4 UX: ship the macro host executable alongside hxhx in dist and make MacroHostClient auto-discover it (env override still supported). This removes the need to set HXHX_MACRO_HOST_EXE for normal usage and makes CI/local workflows closer to the intended distribution layout.

Add an opt-in auto-build path (dev/CI) that, when enabled, invokes scripts/hxhx/build-hxhx-macro-host.sh with the compilation classpaths + macro entrypoints and sets HXHX_MACRO_HOST_EXE automatically. This reduces friction in upstream-shaped runs.

Added deterministic fixture coverage in scripts/test-hxhx-targets.sh.

title: Native frontend lexer: single-quoted literals
description:
Why
- Upstream-ish sources use single-quoted literals and char-like strings; the bootstrap native lexer must tolerate them.

What
- Treat '...'-delimited literals as string tokens (with escapes) in the native lexer protocol.

How
- Extend std/runtime/HxHxNativeLexer.ml to support both "" and '' quoted strings.
acceptance_criteria: - Native lexer can tokenize sources that contain single-quoted literals\n- hxhx --hxhx-parse on those files succeeds

title: Resolver: relative imports + non-recursive traversal
description:
Why
- Upstream code often uses same-package imports like "import MyClass.SubType" inside "package unit;".
- Larger module graphs can overflow the stack if the resolver is recursive.

What
- Support same-package import resolution for uppercase-leading import paths.
- Use an explicit worklist instead of recursion for module graph traversal.

How
- Update packages/hih-compiler/src/ResolverStage.hx accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: - Stage3 resolver can traverse larger graphs safely\n- Same-package imports resolve in upstream-shaped code
